title: Informal Conjecture (Equality in Theorem 1.1 near the zero-rate threshold)
statement_text: We suspect that there may even be equality in the bound $R(q+1; r, s) \geq A_q(r, s) + 1$ when $s$ is sufficiently close to $(1 - 1/q)r$, i.e., $R(q+1; r, s) = A_q(r, s) + 1$, though our methods fall somewhat short of proving this.
context_text: For positive integers $n,r,s$ with $r>s$, the set-coloring Ramsey number $R(n;r,s)$ is the minimum $N$ such that whenever every edge of $K_N$ receives a set of $s$ colors from a palette of $r$ colors, there is a monochromatic $K_n$, i.e. $n$ vertices such that all edges between them share a common color. $A_q(m,d)$ is the maximum size of a code $C\subseteq[q]^m$ in which any two codewords differ in at least $d$ coordinates (Hamming distance at least $d$); by Plotkin, codes of positive rate exist for $d<(1-1/q-\varepsilon)m$ but not for $d\ge(1-1/q)m$. Conlon, Fox, He, Mubayi, Suk and Verstraëte proved that $R(q+1;r,s)\ge A_q(r,s)+1$ for all positive integers $q,r,s$ with $r>s$, and that for fixed $q$ the value $s/r=1-1/q$ is a threshold: $R(q+1;r,s)$ grows exponentially in $r$ below it and is bounded above it. The present paper proves a near-converse close to the threshold: for every $q$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there is $c>0$ such that if $s\le(1-1/q)r$ and $j=(1-1/q)r-s+1$ then $R(q+1;r,s)\le\max((1+\varepsilon)A_q(r,s-cj),\varepsilon s)$, the maximum being unnecessary when $q$ and $r\ge q$ are powers of the same prime. So the two problems are essentially equivalent near the zero-rate threshold, and the authors suspect that the lower bound is exactly tight there.
